title: Sampling And Uncertainty
description: Population vs sample, intervals, and restraint about cause.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can name the population and the sample, compute a named interval in code, and write a claim that does not say 'caused' — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can implement the interval method they named, discuss bias as it applies to this dataset — not a generic list — and keep causal language out unless the design supports it.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently choose an interval that matches the sampling design, state what the interval does and does not cover, and refuse a cause claim the design cannot support.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a confidence interval treated as a causal proof, or a sample treated as the population, and produce a rewrite that names the method and the limit.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's inference note, name a causal verb the design cannot carry (or an unnamed interval), and teach when to stay at association on an unfamiliar study.
